sentences.en: And then he's involved in a series of...
sentences.zh: 然后他卷入了一系列……

sentences.en: I mean, a series of very high-profile events.
sentences.zh: 我是说，一系列非常引人注目的事件。

sentences.en: Obviously, there's the Great Fire of London.
sentences.zh: 显然，有伦敦大火。

sentences.en: There's a plague.
sentences.zh: 还有瘟疫。

sentences.en: There is what some historians traditionally have seen as the birth of politics with the exclusion crisis when Parliament tries to get rid of his...
sentences.zh: 还有一些历史学家传统上认为的政治诞生，即排斥危机，当时议会试图摆脱他的……

sentences.en: to exclude his brother James, Duke of York, from the succession because he's a Catholic and you get the first sort of...
sentences.zh: 试图将他的弟弟约克公爵詹姆斯排除在继承权之外，因为他是天主教徒，然后你看到了第一种……

sentences.en: the first vestiges of kind of...
sentences.zh: 某种……的最初痕迹。

sentences.en: of factional...
sentences.zh: 派系……

sentences.en: of factions coalescing into Whigs and Tories.
sentences.zh: 派系合并成了辉格党和托利党。

sentences.en: But it's also...
sentences.zh: 但这也是……

sentences.en: Charles is...
sentences.zh: 查理是……

sentences.en: And also, also, I should mention, because our Dutch followers are always going on about this,
sentences.zh: 还有，我还得提一下，因为我们的荷兰粉丝总是提起这个，

sentences.en: but apparently there was some war between England and the Dutch Republic that the Dutch won.
sentences.zh: 但据说英格兰和荷兰共和国之间发生过一场战争，而且荷兰赢了。

sentences.en: But that sounds very improbable to me.
sentences.zh: 但这听起来对我来说非常不可信。

sentences.en: I think we should...
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们应该……

sentences.en: I think we should give that no thought at all.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们根本不该考虑那个。

sentences.en: No, listen, we'll just draw a veil over that and not even mention it.
sentences.zh: 不，听着，我们直接把那件事掩盖过去，甚至提都不提。

sentences.en: But he...
sentences.zh: 但他……

sentences.en: But you've been to the Rijksmuseum.
sentences.zh: 但你去过荷兰国立博物馆。

sentences.en: I have, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我去过，没错。

sentences.en: I've seen all those paintings of naval victories that I've never heard of.
sentences.zh: 我看到了所有那些我从未听说过的海军胜利的画作。

sentences.en: Absolutely astonishing.
sentences.zh: 绝对令人震惊。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: You go in, it's just full of paintings of the Dutch beating the English.
sentences.zh: 你走进去，里面全是荷兰人打败英国人的画。

sentences.en: And it's absolutely shocking.
sentences.zh: 这绝对令人震惊。

sentences.en: It should be allowed, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这应该被允许，对吧？

sentences.en: They're just minor skirmishes, aren't they, in English waters, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想那只是英格兰水域里的小规模冲突，对吧。

sentences.en: Ludicrously overinflated.
sentences.zh: 被荒谬地夸大了。

sentences.en: So we don't know what the Dutch are going on about.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道荷兰人在纠结什么。

sentences.en: Anyway, so let's focus on more important things.
sentences.zh: 总之，让我们关注更重要的事情吧。

sentences.en: Because, of course, the most famous thing about
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，关于

sentences.en: Charles II is that he had lots of mistresses.
sentences.zh: 查理二世最著名的事情就是他有很多情妇。

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Nell Gwynn.
sentences.zh: 内尔·格温。

sentences.en: He had, who was, as I recall, from 1066 and all that, was she selling oranges?
sentences.zh: 他有，我记得在《1066和所有那一切》里，她当时是在卖橘子吗？

sentences.en: She was.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And she was one of the top 10 mistresses.
sentences.zh: 她是十大情妇之一。

sentences.en: Was she?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: That you missed, because you were malingering.
sentences.zh: 你错过了，因为你当时在装病。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's Barbara Villiers, Lady Castlemaine.
sentences.zh: 还有芭芭拉·维利尔斯，卡斯尔梅恩夫人。

sentences.en: Yeah, she's great.
sentences.zh: 没错，她很棒。

sentences.en: And Peeps sees her underwear.
sentences.zh: 而且佩皮斯看到了她的内衣。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实看到了。

sentences.en: He's very excited by it, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他对此非常兴奋，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, he is.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是。

sentences.en: There's Louise de Kerouy, the Dutchess of Portsmouth.
sentences.zh: 还有路易丝·德·克鲁阿耶，朴茨茅斯公爵夫人。

sentences.en: And there's Francis Stewart, who resists his importunities.
sentences.zh: 还有弗朗西斯·斯图尔特，她拒绝了他的纠缠。

sentences.en: And she then becomes the model for Britannia on the coinage.
sentences.zh: 后来她成为了硬币上不列颠女神的原型。

sentences.en: That I didn't know.
sentences.zh: 这个我不知道。

sentences.en: That's a good fact.
sentences.zh: 这是个好知识点。

sentences.en: He's also a great scientiSt. So he's very interested in science.
sentences.zh: 他也是一位伟大的科学家。所以他对科学非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: He's instrumental in the Royal Society and in the Royal Observatory.
sentences.zh: 他在皇家学会和皇家天文台的建立中发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: In January 16th, there's a great entry in Peeps's diary, Tom.
sentences.zh: 1月16日，佩皮斯的日记里有一条很棒的记录，汤姆。

sentences.en: Peeps meets Charles II in the park, going for a walk with his brother James.
sentences.zh: 佩皮斯在公园里遇到了查理二世，他正和弟弟詹姆斯散步。

sentences.en: And they go afterwards to the King's Little Elaboratory.
sentences.zh: 之后他们去了国王的小实验室。

sentences.en: So a place where you elaborate.
sentences.zh: 也就是一个进行实验的地方。

sentences.en: So that's where the laboratory comes from.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是实验室（laboratory）一词的由来。

sentences.en: Which I didn't know.
sentences.zh: 这个我不知道。

sentences.en: So you go and elaborate there.
sentences.zh: 所以你去那里进行实验（elaborate）。

sentences.en: Did you know that?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: That's the great thing about this podcaSt. I'm learning new things.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个播客的伟大之处。我正在学习新东西。

sentences.en: We're learning all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在学习。

sentences.en: So Peeps said it was a pretty place.
sentences.zh: 所以佩皮斯说那是个漂亮的地方。

sentences.en: And he there saw a great, I saw a great many chemical glasses and things, but understood none of them.
sentences.zh: 他在那里看到了很多化学玻璃器皿之类的东西，但什么也没看懂。

sentences.en: Which is exactly how I felt as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 这和我十几岁时的感觉一模一样。

sentences.en: Yes, in science lessons.
sentences.zh: 是的，在科学课上。

sentences.en: In science.
sentences.zh: 在科学课上。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Prince Rupert was, Prince Rupert was a keen chemist as well.
sentences.zh: 鲁珀特亲王也是，鲁珀特亲王也是一位热衷的化学家。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: The stewards, they're great scientists.
sentences.zh: 斯图亚特家族，他们是伟大的科学家。

sentences.en: Great scientists.
sentences.zh: 伟大的科学家。

sentences.en: But also, and we should mention this, also a great enthusiast for the slave trade.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我们也应该提到这一点，他也是奴隶贸易的狂热支持者。

sentences.en: Yes, as well.
sentences.zh: 是的，也是。

sentences.en: So Rupert was definitely involved in it.
sentences.zh: 所以鲁珀特绝对参与其中了。

sentences.en: The Charles II involved in the slave trade?
sentences.zh: 查理二世也参与了奴隶贸易？

sentences.en: I think he was.
sentences.zh: 我想他参与了。

sentences.en: I think he was an investor in.
sentences.zh: 我想他是个投资者。

sentences.en: An investor.
sentences.zh: 投资者。

sentences.en: But let's face it, if you're in the Stuart Court in the mid 17th century, everyone's an investor, right?
sentences.zh: 但说实话，如果你身处17世纪中叶的斯图亚特宫廷，每个人都是投资者，对吧？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But I think, I think just mention that because that was something that, that I saw kind of bubbling up.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我认为还是提一下，因为那是我看到有点冒头的事情。

sentences.en: Did you?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: I didn't see that.
sentences.zh: 我没看到。

sentences.en: I don't follow that, that part of Twitter.
sentences.zh: 我不关注推特的那部分内容。

sentences.en: It may amaze you to.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让你感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Well, I just, I was just scanning through, seeing what people were saying about all the various kings.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我只是，我只是在浏览，看看人们对各位国王的评价。

sentences.en: And that was, so looking at the negatives as well as positives.
sentences.zh: 所以既要看负面也要看正面。

sentences.en: And that's, I mean, I guess it's kind of up there with wiping out Irish towns, expelling the Jews and investment in the slave trade are still, you know, they're black marks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想这和摧毁爱尔兰城镇、驱逐犹太人以及投资奴隶贸易一样，都是污点。

sentences.en: The other big thing at the time, of course, so he signs a secret treaty with Louis XIV, in which Louis XIV basically says he will pay him £230,000.
sentences.zh: 当时另一件大事，当然，他与路易十四签署了一份秘密条约，路易十四基本上说会支付他23万英镑。

sentences.en: If Charles, A, joins that war with the Dutch, which is a shambles, which you mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 如果查理A，加入那场对荷兰的战争，那是一场混乱，你之前提到过。

sentences.en: Which we're crossing a veil over.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们掩盖过去的那场。

sentences.en: But secretly, if he converts to Catholicism and will come out as a Catholic and lead England towards Catholicism, something that Charles actually has no intention of doing.
sentences.zh: 但秘密地，如果他改信天主教，并公开成为天主教徒，引导英格兰走向天主教，这是查理实际上根本没打算做的事。

sentences.en: But he does on his deathbed, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他临终时确实改信了，不是吗？

sentences.en: He converts.
sentences.zh: 他改信了。

sentences.en: Supposedly he does on his deathbed, exactly.
sentences.zh: 据说是临终时改信的，确实。

sentences.en: So clearly Charles had, shall we say, papist, papal sympathies.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显查理有，我们姑且说，亲教皇的倾向。

sentences.en: And he takes this money from the French.
sentences.zh: 而且他拿了法国人的钱。

sentences.en: And he's, this has sometimes been held against him by kind of Protestant, Whigish historians,
sentences.zh: 这有时被新教徒、辉格党历史学家所诟病，

sentences.en: but who also see him as conniving and weasel-like and not setting a clear direction and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们也认为他狡诈、像黄鼠狼一样，没有明确的方向等等。

sentences.en: I mean, I would say he's a brilliant politician who, in very troubled times, is actually a very popular king and manages to hold onto his position.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我会说他是一位出色的政治家，在非常动荡的时期，他实际上是一位非常受欢迎的国王，并设法保住了自己的位置。

sentences.en: And yeah, I think he actually...
sentences.zh: 而且是的，我认为他实际上……

sentences.en: Well, he faces the same problem that his father had, which is that he doesn't have the money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他面临着和他父亲一样的问题，那就是他没钱。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Which is why he takes the money from the French.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他拿了法国人的钱。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so rather than kind of, you know, fight a civil war over it, because he's learned from his dad that it's possibly not the best policy.
sentences.zh: 所以与其为了钱打内战，因为他从他父亲那里学到那可能不是最好的策略。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's the thing that Rochester, the Earl of Rochester, who's a fabulously stables, I mean, sensationally rude.
sentences.zh: 这就是罗切斯特伯爵，那个极其……我的意思是，极其粗鲁的人所说的话。

sentences.en: Have you got a quotation from Rochester?
sentences.zh: 你有罗切斯特的引语吗？

sentences.en: I've got the famous one.
sentences.zh: 我有那句名言。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a poem about Charles II that Rochester wrote, which is so rude that I can't read it because we'll lose all our sponsors.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一首罗切斯特写的关于查理二世的诗，太粗鲁了，我不能读，因为我们会失去所有赞助商。

sentences.en: But the concluding line has the famous phrase, restless, he rolls about from whore to whore, a merry monarch, scandalous and poor.
sentences.zh: 但最后一行有那句名言：躁动不安，他在妓女间翻滚，一个快乐的君主，丑闻缠身且贫穷。

sentences.en: And people always remember the merry monarch and the whores and the scandal and things.
sentences.zh: 人们总是记得那个快乐的君主、妓女和丑闻之类的东西。

sentences.en: But it's the poverty, isn't it, really?
sentences.zh: 但真正支撑这些决定的，其实是贫穷，对吧？

sentences.en: That underpins a lot of these decisions.
sentences.zh: 这支撑了很多决定。

sentences.en: But, Tom, he is a merry monarch.
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，他确实是一位快乐的君主。

sentences.en: Like, he, I mean, we haven't talked massively about what it is to be a king.
sentences.zh: 就像，我的意思是，我们还没有深入讨论过作为国王意味着什么。

sentences.en: And so much of it is about presentation, spectacle, performance, iconography.
sentences.zh: 而其中很大一部分是关于展示、奇观、表演和肖像学。

sentences.en: Charles II ticks all of those boxes.
sentences.zh: 查理二世满足了所有这些条件。

sentences.en: He's a very, like Henry VIII, I suppose, or Henry V, you immediately know who he is when you see him.
sentences.zh: 他非常像亨利八世，我想，或者亨利五世，你一看到他立刻就知道他是谁。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Looks like a spaniel, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上长得像只西班牙猎犬。

sentences.en: Spaniel, yes.
sentences.zh: 西班牙猎犬，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, like a King Charles II spaniel.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像查理二世那样的西班牙猎犬。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But he plays the part brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 但他把这个角色演得非常出色。

sentences.en: He's a very canny politician.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常精明的政治家。

sentences.en: He doesn't allow his opponents to outsmart him.
sentences.zh: 他从不让对手胜过自己。

sentences.en: There's a brilliant book by Jenny Oglo called A Gambling Man, where the motif is about cards and playing cards.
sentences.zh: 珍妮·奥格洛写过一本精彩的书叫《赌徒》，书中的主题就是关于纸牌和玩牌。

sentences.en: And Charles II is a brilliant card player.
sentences.zh: 而查理二世是一位出色的牌手。

sentences.en: He knows what card to play at the right time.
sentences.zh: 他知道在什么时候出什么牌。

sentences.en: He always stays in the game, unlike his brother James, who was kicked out after only three years, and unlike his father.
sentences.zh: 他总能留在牌局中，不像他弟弟詹姆斯，仅仅三年就被踢出局，也不像他父亲那样。

sentences.en: So of all the stewards, to me, he's – I mean, I know we're fans of James I on this podcast, but he is the most magnetic and in many ways the most impressive.
sentences.zh: 所以，在所有的斯图亚特王朝君主中，对我来说，他是——我是说，我知道我们在本播客中是詹姆斯一世的粉丝，但他确实是最具魅力，在许多方面也是最令人印象深刻的一位。

sentences.en: Did he not say about James II that no one would murder him, Charles, to make him king?
sentences.zh: 他不是说过关于詹姆斯二世的话吗，说没人会为了让他当国王而谋杀他，查理？

sentences.en: I mean, that's quite wankish.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那话真够混蛋的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Quite wankish.
sentences.zh: 真够混蛋的。

sentences.en: Would you say that of all the monarchs we've talked about, he's the one who's most like Boris?
sentences.zh: 你会说在我们谈论过的所有君主中，他是最像鲍里斯的那一位吗？

sentences.en: That's very good.
sentences.zh: 这评价真好。

sentences.en: Yes, I hadn't thought of that, but he is very Boris-like.
sentences.zh: 是的，我之前没想过，但他确实非常有鲍里斯的风格。

sentences.en: But I was just about to say, he's probably – of all the monarchs on this podcast, who would you go for a drink with?
sentences.zh: 但我正想说，他可能是——在本播客提到的所有君主中，你会想和谁一起去喝一杯？

sentences.en: Charles II's got to be up there.
sentences.zh: 查理二世肯定算一个。

sentences.en: Yeah, you'd be frightened to have a drink with Edward I, wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 是啊，和爱德华一世一起喝酒你会感到害怕，对吧？

sentences.en: I wouldn't have a drink with –
sentences.zh: 我才不会和——

sentences.en: Spill his pint.
sentences.zh: 会洒了他的品脱啤酒。

sentences.en: I wouldn't go for a drink with Richard the Lionheart or something.
sentences.zh: 我不会和狮心王理查之类的人去喝酒。

sentences.en: I mean, he wouldn't even tell me.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他甚至都不会告诉我。

sentences.en: Smacking you on the – that'd be terrifying.
sentences.zh: 打你的脸——那太可怕了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or Knute.
sentences.zh: 或者克努特大帝。

sentences.en: I mean –
sentences.zh: 我是说——

sentences.en: Well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: A beachside –
sentences.zh: 海滩边的——

sentences.en: A beachside cocktail.
sentences.zh: 海滩边的鸡尾酒。

sentences.en: A beachside barbecue.
sentences.zh: 海滩边的烧烤。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Anyway, we're waffling.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们在胡扯了。

sentences.en: Let's – Charles II, I think quarterfinals is about right.
sentences.zh: 让我们——查理二世，我觉得进四分之一决赛差不多是合适的。

sentences.en: I actually expected him to reach the semis because of the sheer magnetism of the very monarch, but he didn't.
sentences.zh: 我其实期望他能进入半决赛，因为这位君主本身就有着纯粹的魅力，但他没能做到。

sentences.en: Crashed out to Elizabeth I.
sentences.zh: 被伊丽莎白一世淘汰了。

sentences.en: Maybe with a different draw, he could have gone further.
sentences.zh: 也许换个抽签结果，他能走得更远。

sentences.en: However, he didn't get a different draw.
sentences.zh: 然而，他没能换个抽签结果。

sentences.en: So the next monarch to crash out was Edward III.
sentences.zh: 所以下一位被淘汰的君主是爱德华三世。

sentences.en: Against Athelstan.
sentences.zh: 输给了阿塞尔斯坦。

sentences.en: Been by Athelstan.
sentences.zh: 被阿塞尔斯坦淘汰的。

sentences.en: So Edward III, he was king for 50 years.
sentences.zh: 所以爱德华三世，他当了50年的国王。

sentences.en: I mean, by medieval standards, a colossal, absolutely colossal ring.
sentences.zh: 我是说，以中世纪的标准来看，这是一个巨大的，绝对巨大的统治期。

sentences.en: Well, he was 14 when he became king.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他继位时才14岁。

sentences.en: He was, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 确实是，不是吗？

sentences.en: So his mum and her partner, her lover –
sentences.zh: 所以他的母亲和她的伴侣，她的情人——

sentences.en: Do that again?
sentences.zh: 能再说一遍吗？

sentences.en: That was very good.
sentences.zh: 那句说得真好。

sentences.en: – lover – had disposed of dad, Edward II.
sentences.zh: ——情人——除掉了他的父亲，爱德华二世。

sentences.en: Yes, horrifically.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常恐怖地。

sentences.en: Unpleasantly.
sentences.zh: 非常令人不快地。

sentences.en: Everyone knew, so we won't go on about it.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，所以我们就不多说了。

sentences.en: Oh, you were just about to.
sentences.zh: 噢，你刚才正要说呢。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was.
sentences.zh: 是的，我正要说。

sentences.en: I was about to say – well, it's a poker, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我正要说——嗯，是火钳，对吧？

sentences.en: It's the insertion of a poker.
sentences.zh: 是插入火钳。

sentences.en: Okay, that's the claim, but I think that a lot of more serious, scrupulous historians say that probably is just a total invention.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是种说法，但我认为许多更严肃、更严谨的历史学家认为这可能完全是虚构的。

sentences.en: So we'll say it happened.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就当它发生过吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they're Roger Mortimer and Isabella, and Edward basically turns against them when he grows up a little bit more, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他们是罗杰·莫蒂默和伊莎贝拉，爱德华在长大一点后基本上就反过来对付他们了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And gets rid of them, and Roger Mortimer is hanged, I think.
sentences.zh: 并除掉了他们，我想罗杰·莫蒂默被绞死了。

sentences.en: So I always loved Edward III.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直很喜欢爱德华三世。

sentences.en: I think we talked about this before, the Conan Doyle's novels about chivalry.
sentences.zh: 我想我们之前谈过这个，柯南·道尔关于骑士精神的小说。

sentences.en: Isn't it the White Company?
sentences.zh: 是《白衣队》吗？

sentences.en: White Company, Sir Nigel, which at the time didn't seem funny to him at all.
sentences.zh: 《白衣队》、《奈杰尔爵士》，在当时看来对他一点也不好笑。

sentences.en: I absolutely loved them, and Edward III is such a kind of dashing figure in them.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢它们，爱德华三世在书中是一个非常潇洒的人物。

sentences.en: He's a model of a –
sentences.zh: 他是——的典范。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But do you not think he's slightly – to people who are not experts on the 14th century, Edward III just seems like a slightly generic, bearded English king.
sentences.zh: 但你不觉得他稍微有点——对于那些不是14世纪专家的人来说，爱德华三世看起来就像一个稍微有点大众化的、留着胡子的英国国王吗？

sentences.en: He fights the French.
sentences.zh: 他与法国人作战。

sentences.en: He's very chivalrous.
sentences.zh: 他非常有骑士精神。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But what's wrong with that?
sentences.zh: 但这有什么错吗？

sentences.en: No, nothing is wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 不，这没什么错。

sentences.en: Surely you're not complaining about that.
sentences.zh: 你肯定不是在抱怨这个吧。

sentences.en: I'm not complaining, but I find him quite hard to pin down what's distinctive about him.
sentences.zh: 我不是在抱怨，但我发现很难确定他有什么独特之处。

sentences.en: Well, so he lays claim to the French throne.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他宣称拥有法国王位。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Again, absolutely unjustifiably, but what the hell?
sentences.zh: 同样，完全没有正当理由，但那又怎样呢？

sentences.en: They've confiscated Aquitaine, haven't they, the French?
sentences.zh: 法国人没收了阿基坦，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's what he – that's the pretext for all this, or that's the trigger.
sentences.zh: 这就是他——这就是这一切的借口，或者说是导火索。

sentences.en: Well, no, he's claiming – it's all to do with the Salic Law.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，他声称——这都与萨利克继承法有关。

sentences.en: Well, there's a bit of that as well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也有点那方面的因素，是的。

sentences.en: It's said through the female line, which, according to French law, doesn't count, and he says it does.
sentences.zh: 据说通过母系继承，根据法国法律，这不作数，但他坚持说作数。

sentences.en: Anyway, it's all just an excuse to have a massive romp, and so the English defeat the French at the naval battle of Sluice.
sentences.zh: 总之，这都只是进行一场大规模狂欢的借口，于是英国人在斯勒伊斯海战中击败了法国人。

sentences.en: And then they have the Battle of Cressy, where they unleash the longbow.
sentences.zh: 然后他们进行了克雷西战役，在那里他们动用了长弓。

sentences.en: Great moment.
sentences.zh: 伟大的时刻。

sentences.en: So – and it's kind of heartwarming.
sentences.zh: 所以——这有点令人暖心。

sentences.en: It's the union between stirring chivalrous knights and kind of horny-handed Sandbrook figures.
sentences.zh: 这是激动人心的骑士精神与桑德布鲁克笔下那种粗手粗脚的人物之间的结合。

sentences.en: Yeoman.
sentences.zh: 自耕农。

sentences.en: Yeoman, I think is the word.
sentences.zh: 我想应该是自耕农这个词。

sentences.en: With their longbows.
sentences.zh: 带着他们的长弓。

sentences.en: And it's all utterly chivalrous.
sentences.zh: 而且这一切都极其具有骑士精神。

sentences.en: And the Black Prince, his son, it's his first big battle.
sentences.zh: 还有黑太子，他的儿子，这是他的第一场大战。

sentences.en: He's coming under pressure.
sentences.zh: 他正承受着压力。

sentences.en: People come and ask Edward III, should we go to his rescue?
sentences.zh: 有人来问爱德华三世，我们应该去救他吗？

sentences.en: And he says, no, let the boy win his spurs.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，让这孩子自己去赢得荣誉。

sentences.en: And he does win his spurs.
sentences.zh: 他也确实赢得了荣誉。

sentences.en: Great moment.
sentences.zh: 伟大的时刻。

sentences.en: And he kills the blind king of Bohemia and takes his Ich die in, I serve, his motto, which is still the Prince of Wales motto to this day.
sentences.zh: 他杀死了波希米亚的盲王，并夺取了他的座右铭“Ich dien”（我服侍），这至今仍是威尔士亲王的座右铭。

sentences.en: And it's all utterly chivalrous.
sentences.zh: 而且这一切都极其具有骑士精神。

sentences.en: And then due course, the Black Prince wins the Battle of Poitiers as well in exactly the same way.
sentences.zh: 随后，黑太子也以同样的方式赢得了普瓦捷战役。

sentences.en: And he actually captures the French king.
sentences.zh: 而且他实际上俘虏了法国国王。

sentences.en: Edward III has captured both the Scottish and the French king.
sentences.zh: 爱德华三世俘虏了苏格兰和法国两位国王。

sentences.en: You know, it's all – you know, what's not to like?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这一切——你知道，有什么不好的呢？

sentences.en: It's all utterly chivalrous and heroic.
sentences.zh: 这一切都极其具有骑士精神和英雄气概。

sentences.en: However, there are two massive downsides.
sentences.zh: 然而，有两个巨大的负面影响。

sentences.en: One is the Black Death, which obviously is not good news.
sentences.zh: 一个是黑死病，这显然不是什么好消息。

sentences.en: That's not really his fault, though.
sentences.zh: 不过那其实不是他的错。

sentences.en: I mean, he can't –
sentences.zh: 我是说，他不能——

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不是。

sentences.en: He should have locked down earlier.
sentences.zh: 他本应该早点封城的。

sentences.en: Well, but I mean, it's like COVID kind of interrupting the sports fixtures.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我的意思是，这就像新冠疫情打断了体育赛事一样。

sentences.en: It interrupts the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 它打断了百年战争。

sentences.en: So they have to kind of stop the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不得不暂停百年战争。

sentences.en: You know, we'll play it in kind of empty stadiuMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们会在空荡荡的体育场里比赛。

sentences.en: Behind closed doors.
sentences.zh: 闭门比赛。

sentences.en: Yes, behind closed doors.
sentences.zh: 是的，闭门比赛。

sentences.en: So the Battle of Poitiers before the Black Death and Battle of Poitiers comes, you know, they're emerging out of lockdown.
sentences.zh: 所以黑死病之前的普瓦捷战役，以及黑死病之后的普瓦捷战役，你知道，他们正走出封锁。

sentences.en: But the other thing that stands against Edward III is that he ends up very kind of senile and under the thumb of a sinister mistress called Alice Perez.
sentences.zh: 但另一件不利于爱德华三世的事情是，他最终变得非常老糊涂，并受到一位名叫爱丽丝·佩雷斯的邪恶情妇的控制。

sentences.en: Alice Perez.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝·佩雷斯。

sentences.en: Is she sinister or is that just put about by her?
sentences.zh: 她是邪恶的，还是那只是别人对她的诋毁？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's all put about – I don't know.
sentences.zh: 是的，都是诋毁——我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, but there's the definite sense that actually, a bit like with Henry V,
sentences.zh: 我是说，但确实有一种感觉，实际上，有点像亨利五世那样，

sentences.en: the whole idea of invading France is basically a disastrous idea and that no matter how successful some of the battles might be,
sentences.zh: 入侵法国的整个想法基本上是个灾难性的主意，无论某些战役可能多么成功，

sentences.en: the whole thing in the long run will lead to a kind of meltdown, which is what happens in England because peasants revolt, misery.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，整件事都会导致某种崩溃，这正是英格兰发生的事情，因为农民起义，苦难重重。

sentences.en: But, Tom, it's a very important reign, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，这是一个非常重要的统治时期，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it sees the triumph of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 因为它见证了骑士精神的胜利。

sentences.en: It sees English being used in law courts and in Parliament.
sentences.zh: 它见证了英语在法庭和议会中的使用。

sentences.en: Chaucer, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然还有乔叟。

sentences.en: So it feels like – is it wrong to see it as a – well, how can it be a golden age when a third of the population has been killed by the Black Death?
sentences.zh: 所以感觉像是——把它看作一个黄金时代是错的吗？毕竟三分之一的人口死于黑死病？

sentences.en: But people do see it as – I mean, obviously, Arthur Conan Doyle saw it as a bit of a golden age, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 但人们确实把它看作——我是说，显然，阿瑟·柯南·道尔把它看作是一个黄金时代，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I think it kind of merges with a vague, hazy idea of King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得它与关于亚瑟王的模糊、朦胧的想法融合在了一起。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Prasar said, didn't he, that Edward III was such a king as had not been seen since the days of King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 普拉萨尔说过，不是吗，爱德华三世是自亚瑟王时代以来从未见过的国王。

sentences.en: Yes, and there's the whole – he establishes the Order of the Garter.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有整个——他建立了嘉德勋章。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Oni swaki maliponce.
sentences.zh: 心怀邪念者蒙羞。

sentences.en: Evil be to he who evil thinks.
sentences.zh: 心怀邪念者蒙羞。

sentences.en: Honey, you've lost your garter, as 1066 transcribes it.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的，你丢了你的吊袜带，正如1066年所记载的那样。

sentences.en: So I think there's a kind of a general – a bit like Henry V, there's a kind of aureate glow around it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有一种普遍的——有点像亨利五世，周围有一种金色的光环。

sentences.en: But also when I think of it, I think of it as – so if I'm kind of imagining Edward III's reign, I'm thinking a bright, sunny morning, glorious midday,
sentences.zh: 但当我想到它时，我也把它想象成——如果我是在想象爱德华三世的统治，我想象的是一个明亮、阳光明媚的早晨，辉煌的正午，

sentences.en: and then the clouds start to roll in.
sentences.zh: 然后乌云开始聚集。

sentences.en: And plague.
sentences.zh: 还有瘟疫。

sentences.en: And plague, and it all goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 还有瘟疫，一切都出了问题。

sentences.en: So the historian Norman Cantor said of Edward III, he was an avaricious and sadistic thug.
sentences.zh: 所以历史学家诺曼·坎特这样评价爱德华三世：他是一个贪婪且残暴的暴徒。

sentences.en: I'm sure he was.
sentences.zh: 我相信他是。

sentences.en: But that's what people wanted, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但那正是人们想要的，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's the mark of great kingship in the medieval period.
sentences.zh: 那是中世纪伟大君主制的标志。

sentences.en: To booty for your mates and bashing the French.
sentences.zh: 为了给同伙掠夺战利品，顺便痛打法国人。

sentences.en: Which, again, I think kind of highlights the way that in this World Cup, we are – every monarch has to be judged by the standards of the age in which they rule.
sentences.zh: 这再次凸显了我在本届世界杯中一直强调的观点：每一位君主都必须以他们所处时代的标准来衡量。

sentences.en: And I suppose ultimately what's being judged is whether they're iconic.
sentences.zh: 我想最终评判的是他们是否具有标志性意义。

sentences.en: Like, yeah, I think that's probably true.
sentences.zh: 没错，我想这大概是真的。

sentences.en: So talking of avaricious and sadistic thugs, we're now on to the semifinals.
sentences.zh: 说到贪婪和残暴的暴徒，我们现在进入半决赛了。

sentences.en: And the first semifinal saw Athelstan.
sentences.zh: 第一场半决赛是埃塞尔斯坦的比赛。

sentences.en: It was a sort of – you know, it was an Anglo-Saxon-Norman rematch, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 那算是一场……你知道，那是一场盎格鲁-撒克逊人与诺曼人的重赛，对吧？

sentences.en: It was Athelstan against William the Conqueror.
sentences.zh: 那是埃塞尔斯坦对阵征服者威廉。

sentences.en: At that point when I saw Jonathan Wilson make the draw, it was blindingly obvious to me that Athelstan would make the final.
sentences.zh: 当看到乔纳森·威尔逊进行抽签时，我立刻就明白埃塞尔斯坦会进入决赛。

sentences.en: Because William the Conqueror is a man who is respected but, I think, fair to say, not loved.
sentences.zh: 因为征服者威廉是一个受人尊敬，但说实话，并不受人爱戴的人。

sentences.en: No, and I'm amazed, actually, that he got this far.
sentences.zh: 没错，而且我真的很惊讶他竟然能走到这一步。

sentences.en: And I think it's really interesting, the fact he did get this far, what it says about – well, about how Hastings is viewed, actually.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他能走到这一步非常耐人寻味，这说明了……嗯，说明了人们实际上是如何看待黑斯廷斯战役的。

sentences.en: But he's been rewarded here.
sentences.zh: 但他在这里得到了回报。

sentences.en: Nobody – I mean, if you asked English people in the streets, do you wish the Anglo-Saxons had won the Battle of Hastings, they would probably say yes, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 没人——我是说，如果你问街上的英国人，你希望盎格鲁-撒克逊人在黑斯廷斯战役中获胜吗？他们可能会说愿意，不是吗？

sentences.en: The Anglo-Saxons are romantic.
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊人很浪漫。

sentences.en: They are the underdogs in the Battle of Hastings.
sentences.zh: 他们是黑斯廷斯战役中的弱势一方。

sentences.en: But he is being – he's the sort of Margaret Thatcher of this competition.
sentences.zh: 但他现在……他是这场比赛中的玛格丽特·撒切尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, but if you said we lost the Battle of Hastings, I don't think people would say that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但如果你说我们输掉了黑斯廷斯战役，我不认为人们会那样说。

sentences.en: I mean, you might say – you know, an English person might say we won the Battle of Waterloo or we won the Battle of Britain.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你可能会说……你知道，一个英国人可能会说我们赢得了滑铁卢战役或不列颠战役。

sentences.en: But would we say we lost the Battle of Hastings?
sentences.zh: 但我们会说我们输掉了黑斯廷斯战役吗？

sentences.en: I don't think we would because I think we recognise that, actually, what William brought was so formative for England that it's become a part of what it is to be English.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们会，因为我认为我们意识到，威廉带来的东西对英国具有如此深远的塑造作用，以至于它已经成为英国人身份的一部分。

sentences.en: And obviously, that's the case with the monarchy.
sentences.zh: 显然，君主制也是如此。

sentences.en: The monarchy is more Norman, perhaps, than it is Anglo-Saxon.
sentences.zh: 君主制与其说是盎格鲁-撒克逊的，不如说是诺曼的。

sentences.en: You mean because it's – the Anglo-Saxon monarchy was more – what?
sentences.zh: 你是说因为它是……盎格鲁-撒克逊的君主制更……什么？

sentences.en: Was more elective, more consensual, more low-key?
sentences.zh: 更倾向于选举制、更讲究共识、更低调？

sentences.en: No, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: The antiquity and the dignity of the Anglo-Saxon monarchy is very, very important to William.
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊君主制的古老和尊严对威廉来说非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: It's part of the loot of England.
sentences.zh: 这是英国战利品的一部分。

sentences.en: It's part of what he wants.
sentences.zh: 这是他想要的一部分。

sentences.en: The fact that it is, dare I say, sacral.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我敢说，它是神圣的。

sentences.en: You become an – as Duke of Normandy, he's not an anointed ruler.
sentences.zh: 作为诺曼底公爵，他不是受膏的统治者。

sentences.en: As King of England, he is.
sentences.zh: 但作为英国国王，他是。

sentences.en: So that's very important.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常重要。

sentences.en: But the fact that, basically, we date kings from 1066.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，我们基本上是从1066年开始计算国王的。

sentences.en: So we've said that, you know, there are three King Edwards before Edward I, but he is the first Edward.
sentences.zh: 所以我们说，你知道，爱德华一世之前有三位爱德华国王，但他才是第一位爱德华。

sentences.en: I think it reflects the fact that, essentially, we see William as the founder of the English monarchy in a way that obviously is ahistorical,
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了一个事实，即我们本质上将威廉视为英国君主制的奠基人，尽管这显然是不符合历史的，

sentences.en: but reflects a kind of deep truth of just how significant William's reign is.
sentences.zh: 但这反映了一种深刻的真相，即威廉的统治是多么重要。

sentences.en: And that, therefore, in a sense, he is seen as not just a kind of alien invader, perhaps in the way that Knut is, but as a legitimate King of England.
sentences.zh: 因此，在某种意义上，他被视为合法的英国国王，而不是像克努特那样被视为外来的入侵者。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是真的。

sentences.en: It's partly because of the Doomsday Book, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为《末日审判书》，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because the Doomsday Book is seen as one of the foundational texts of English government and of English identity, actually.
sentences.zh: 因为《末日审判书》被视为英国政府和英国身份认同的奠基性文献之一。

sentences.en: Also, I think, I mean, the kind of the castles that he and his followers planned across England, they've kind of also become representative of the Middle Ages for people.
sentences.zh: 此外，我认为，他和他的追随者在英国各地规划的城堡，也已经成为人们心目中中世纪的代表。

sentences.en: So if you have a castle and the great cathedrals of which Durham would be the kind of the first,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一座城堡，还有伟大的大教堂，其中达勒姆大教堂是第一座，

sentences.en: that these for most of us, I think, are kind of visual symbols of what England is.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于我们大多数人来说，这些是英国视觉上的象征。

sentences.en: And because we don't have Anglo-Saxon equivalents, that's another reason, I think, why the Anglo-Saxon period is so much more shadowy.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我们没有盎格鲁-撒克逊时期的同类建筑，我认为这是盎格鲁-撒克逊时期显得如此模糊的另一个原因。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，我肯定。

sentences.en: I think that's very true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常正确。

sentences.en: I think there's also, with William, though, there's the issue of his, shall we say, his bastardy.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为威廉还有一个问题，那就是他的，我们姑且称之为，私生子身份。

sentences.en: So he was called William the Bastard because he was illegitimate, and he seemed to have behaved like a bastard.
sentences.zh: 他被称为“杂种威廉”，因为他是私生子，而且他似乎表现得像个混蛋。

sentences.en: He was a bastard, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他是个混蛋，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Harrying northerners, smiting people.
sentences.zh: 蹂躏北方人，打击异己。

sentences.en: Well, again, so a definite sense from Twitter engagements that people in the North have not forgotten.
sentences.zh: 嗯，再说一次，从推特的互动来看，北方人确实没有忘记。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, it was a kind of near-genocidal repression of rebellion in the North.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，那是一种近乎种族灭绝式的对北方叛乱的镇压。

sentences.en: I mean, can you make a case for him and say he's ruthless and that's what he has to be?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你能为他辩护，说他冷酷无情，而他必须如此吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he lives in a ruthless age where you win by the sword, and if you don't, you die.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他生活在一个冷酷的时代，你靠剑获胜，如果你不这样做，你就会死。

sentences.en: I mean, that's surely the case you'd make, that he's a strong leader, and any successful regime in the 11th century, you have to be really stern.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这肯定是你想要表达的观点，他是一位强有力的领导者，在11世纪，任何成功的政权都必须非常严厉。

sentences.en: Yes, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: But even his own followers, so Aldrich Vitalis, who's very admiring of him generally, says of the harrowing of the North that with this, I cannot, you know, I can't justify this.
sentences.zh: 但即使是他的追随者，比如奥德里克·维塔利斯，他通常非常钦佩威廉，但也说关于蹂躏北方的事，这一点我无法，你知道，我无法为之辩护。

sentences.en: This was a terrible thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件可怕的事情。

sentences.en: So even by the standards of his own time, he's seen as repressive, autocratic.
sentences.zh: 所以即使以他那个时代的标准来看，他也被视为压迫性的、专制的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think the great abbey he builds on the site of Hastings, the Battle of Hastings, is also a monument to that,
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我认为他在黑斯廷斯战役遗址上建造的宏伟修道院也是对此的一种纪念，

sentences.en: because that's built as a way to try and expiate the crime that he committed in killing so many people.
sentences.zh: 因为那是为了赎罪，为了弥补他杀害那么多人所犯下的罪行。

sentences.en: So I think that kind of strange, which you also have in Henry V, the strange combination of kind of martial brutality and piety, you absolutely get in William.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那种奇怪的组合，你在亨利五世身上也能看到，那种军事上的残暴与虔诚的奇怪结合，在威廉身上绝对存在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And neither of those are very popular qualities at the moment.
sentences.zh: 而且这两种品质在当下都不太受欢迎。

sentences.en: But that's why the story that everybody enjoys about William is his funeral.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么每个人都喜欢关于威廉的那个故事——他的葬礼。

sentences.en: So he's died in Normandy, and his body is sort of expanded with gas, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 他在诺曼底去世了，他的尸体因为气体膨胀了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that right?
sentences.zh: 不是这样吗？

sentences.en: That he's sort of swollen.
sentences.zh: 他肿胀起来了。

sentences.en: They're trying to shove his body into the coffin that's basically too small for it.
sentences.zh: 他们试图把他的尸体塞进一个太小的棺材里。

sentences.en: He's become an enormous fellow.
sentences.zh: 他变成了一个巨大的家伙。

sentences.en: They shove him in, and he bursts, and his entrails fall out with a terrible stench.
sentences.zh: 他们把他塞进去，结果他爆开了，内脏流了出来，恶臭难闻。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And everybody doesn't really run out of the church in horror or something.
sentences.zh: 大家并没有真的惊恐地跑出教堂什么的。

sentences.en: So it's a very undignified end.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常不体面的结局。

sentences.en: Harold Godwinson's revenge, I think we can call it.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可以称之为哈罗德·戈德温森的复仇。

sentences.en: And he's buried next to his wife, Matilda, who everyone says is very small, but actually wasn't.
sentences.zh: 他被安葬在他妻子玛蒂尔达旁边，大家都说她很矮，但实际上并不是。

sentences.en: Wasn't she?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: No, she wasn't, apparently.
sentences.zh: 不，显然不是。

sentences.en: Why do people say it then?
sentences.zh: 那为什么人们这么说呢？

sentences.en: Because their graves got rifled in the French Revolution, and I think bits have got kind of loSt.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的坟墓在法国大革命期间被洗劫了，我想有些部分丢失了。

sentences.en: So people thought she was basically four foot.
sentences.zh: 所以人们以为她只有四英尺高。

sentences.en: She was an absolute midget.
sentences.zh: 她简直是个侏儒。

sentences.en: Well, they don't realise that the rest of her is missing.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们没意识到她身体的其他部分不见了。

sentences.en: Well, they've kind of gone back and worked out that actually she was of absolutely average height.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们回去研究后发现，她实际上是绝对的平均身高。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, this is fascinating stuff.
sentences.zh: 这真是太迷人了。

sentences.en: An average-heighted woman, not a small one.
sentences.zh: 一个平均身高的女人，不是个矮子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we have one other semi-final loser, don't we?
sentences.zh: 所以我们还有另一位半决赛输家，对吧？

sentences.en: So we had the Elizabeth Derby, Elizabeth I against Elizabeth II.
sentences.zh: 我们有伊丽莎白德比，伊丽莎白一世对阵伊丽莎白二世。

sentences.en: Yet again, Elizabeth I won an absolutely crushing victory.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白一世再次取得了压倒性的胜利。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth II.
sentences.zh: 还有伊丽莎白二世。

sentences.en: Now, you said that she'd done nothing.
sentences.zh: 现在，你说她什么都没做。

sentences.en: I mean, she hasn't done nothing, but she's done little by comparison with her previous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她不是什么都没做，但与前任相比，她做得很少。

sentences.en: But she's done nothing in a positive way.
sentences.zh: 但她在积极的方面什么都没做。

sentences.en: Hasn't she?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She's been positively boring.
sentences.zh: 她表现得非常无聊。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She's been very canny in her boringness, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为她在这种无聊中表现得非常精明。

sentences.en: And she has, you know, God, I mean, I do so many kind of Channel 5 talking head things about the 20th century monarchy.
sentences.zh: 而且她已经，你知道，天哪，我做了那么多关于20世纪君主制的第五频道访谈节目。

sentences.en: My heart really isn't in saying yet again.
sentences.zh: 我真的不想再重复这些了。

sentences.en: Okay, well, go on.
sentences.zh: 好吧，继续说。

sentences.en: Well, just what's your take on that?
sentences.zh: 那么，你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: Saying yet again, you know, she's managed the – she's navigated the shoals.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，你知道，她成功地……她渡过了难关。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Great friends with Harold Wilson, you know, Silver Jubilee.
sentences.zh: 和哈罗德·威尔逊是好朋友，你知道，银禧庆典。

sentences.en: I could do it.
sentences.zh: 我能做到。

sentences.en: To be honest, I'd just hear my own voice droning in my sleep.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我会在睡梦中听到自己单调的声音。

sentences.en: My agent will be absolutely livid with me for saying this, doing myself out of, you know, 101 top Elizabeth II moments on Channel 4 in 2027 or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我的经纪人会因为我说这些而气疯的，这让我失去了在2027年第四频道做《伊丽莎白二世的101个高光时刻》之类的机会。

sentences.en: Anyway, do you want to talk about the Queen, Tom?
sentences.zh: 总之，你想谈谈女王吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Well, I think – so if we say we have to judge monarchs by, you know, if we're judging their success by the standards of the age in which they live,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想……如果我们说我们必须以他们所处时代的标准来评判君主，如果我们以他们生活的时代的标准来评判他们的成功，

sentences.en: I would say that it's a case for saying Elizabeth II is the most successful monarch Britain's ever had.
sentences.zh: 我会说，有理由认为伊丽莎白二世是英国历史上最成功的君主。

sentences.en: Well, if you're judging – but you're judging by such different standards, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你在评判……但你评判的标准太不同了，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean –
sentences.zh: 我是说……

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，当然。

sentences.en: So she hasn't changed the course of English history.
sentences.zh: 所以她没有改变英国历史的进程。

sentences.en: She hasn't won – you know, hasn't defeated the French, hasn't changed the religion or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 她没有赢得……你知道，没有打败法国人，没有改变宗教信仰之类的。

sentences.en: But her role as a constitutional monarch has been to serve as a figurehead for the nation.
sentences.zh: 但她作为立宪君主的角色是作为国家的象征。

sentences.en: You should do these documentaries instead of me.
sentences.zh: 你应该代替我做这些纪录片。

sentences.en: I know I should.
sentences.zh: 我知道我应该。

sentences.en: Because for me, I haven't actually really thought about this before.
sentences.zh: 因为对我来说，我之前并没有真正思考过这个问题。

sentences.en: So for me, it's all fresh.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这一切都是新鲜的。

sentences.en: So you can just kind of barrack me on the side.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在旁边给我提点建议。

sentences.en: But what you'd say about the decades of her reign is that they have been remarkably convulsive.
sentences.zh: 但你会说她统治的几十年里，英国经历了惊人的动荡。

sentences.en: It's hard to think of a time where people's understanding of, say, morals or ethics have changed so radically.
sentences.zh: 很难想象还有什么时期，人们对道德或伦理的理解发生了如此剧烈的变化。

sentences.en: And we've discussed that before.
sentences.zh: 我们之前讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, that's culturally convulsive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是文化上的剧变。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 得了吧。

sentences.en: I think attitudes to sex, to gender, to race have changed so profoundly.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对性、性别、种族的态度发生了如此深刻的变化。

sentences.en: And I think also what's interesting is that they have changed in ways that objectively should be very destabilizing to the idea of a hereditary monarchy.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有趣的是，它们的变化方式客观上应该对世袭君主制的理念产生极大的破坏性。

sentences.en: Because the idea of a kind of authority and privilege oppressing those who historically have been underprivileged has become an absolute no-no.
sentences.zh: 因为那种权威和特权压迫历史上弱势群体的观念已经变得绝对不可接受了。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what kind of has driven the feminist revolution, the giving to gay people of basically rights equivalent to heterosexual people, the anxieties about racism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是推动女权主义革命、赋予同性恋者与异性恋者基本同等权利、以及对种族主义的焦虑的原因。

sentences.en: That all of these, you would have thought,
sentences.zh: 你会认为所有这些，

sentences.en: would be threatening to the idea of the fact that our head of state rules by virtue of her descent from a long line of monarchs who ultimately go back to Woden.
sentences.zh: 都会威胁到这样一个事实：我们的国家元首统治是因为她继承了最终可以追溯到沃登的一长串君主血统。

sentences.en: You know, there's nothing obvious about the fact that people would continue to accept this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们会继续接受这一点并不是理所当然的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think by and large, people do.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为总的来说，人们接受了。

sentences.en: And so by that standard, I would say that Elizabeth's achievement has been astonishing.
sentences.zh: 所以按照这个标准，我会说伊丽莎白的成就令人惊叹。

sentences.en: And I think the reason why she's been successful isn't just because she's, you know, she's accepted that being boring is basically what her job has been,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为她之所以成功，不仅仅是因为她接受了无聊基本上就是她的工作，

sentences.en: but also that she really believes it.
sentences.zh: 还因为她真的相信这一点。

sentences.en: She takes it very, very seriously.
sentences.zh: 她非常、非常认真地对待它。

sentences.en: And I think that it's absolutely essential for the success of monarchy that monarchs themselves take what they're doing very, very seriously.
sentences.zh: 我认为君主制要成功，君主本人必须非常、非常认真地对待他们所做的事情，这是绝对必要的。

sentences.en: Yeah, you couldn't be a flippant monarch, could you?
sentences.zh: 是的，你不能做一个轻浮的君主，对吧？

sentences.en: You couldn't be a kind of Charles II type monarch now.
sentences.zh: 你现在不能做一个查理二世那样的君主。

sentences.en: You have to take it seriously.
sentences.zh: 你必须认真对待。

sentences.en: You have to be earnest about it.
sentences.zh: 你必须对此表现得诚恳。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth II really does.
sentences.zh: 而伊丽莎白二世确实是这样。

sentences.en: She really does think that she's been appointed by God, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她确实认为自己是上帝任命的。

sentences.en: And that's what makes me wonder whether the institutional will last very long after her.
sentences.zh: 这让我怀疑在她之后，这个体制还能维持多久。

sentences.en: I always think it will.
sentences.zh: 我总觉得它能维持下去。

sentences.en: I think, well, let's not get into prognostications for the future.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，好吧，我们还是别去预测未来了。

sentences.en: But what I would say is that one of the other things that we've talked about is how children can be problematic for reigning kings.
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，我们之前讨论过的另一件事是，孩子对在位君主来说可能是个麻烦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think Charles is fine.
sentences.zh: 我觉得查尔斯没问题。

sentences.en: But I think, for instance, Andrew is a shocker.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，比如安德鲁，简直是个奇葩。

sentences.en: I think he's like a kind of great cancer at the heart of people's acceptance of monarchy, because a kind of thick, entitled perv is not a good look for any king, you know,
sentences.zh: 我觉得他就像是人们接受君主制核心中的一颗毒瘤，因为一个愚蠢、自以为是的色狼，对任何国王来说都不是什么好形象，你知道的，

sentences.en: even in the 60th century.
sentences.zh: 即使是在60世纪也是如此。

sentences.en: I think English history has been littered with thick, entitled pervs.
sentences.zh: 我觉得英国历史上到处都是愚蠢、自以为是的色狼。

sentences.en: I know, but generally they haven't gone down well.
sentences.zh: 我知道，但通常他们都没什么好下场。

sentences.en: So I think Andrew is a kind of reminder to people of what monarchy can serve up to you.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为安德鲁提醒了人们君主制会带来什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think what I would say in sort of agreement with you is, first of all, the Queen is probably the most popular monarch Britain has ever had, because by her nature,
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我同意你的一点是，首先，女王可能是英国有史以来最受欢迎的君主，因为就她的天性而言，

sentences.en: she's not divisive.
sentences.zh: 她不会制造分裂。

sentences.en: I mean, she hasn't had to make the divisive choices that a previous, more powerful monarch would have had to have made.
sentences.zh: 我是说，她不必做出以前那些更有权势的君主所必须做出的那种分裂性的选择。

sentences.en: So her prime ministers have been divisive, but she hasn't.
sentences.zh: 所以她的首相们制造了分裂，但她没有。

sentences.en: And she probably leaves the monarchy on firmer foundations than would have seemed possible under any other post-1950s monarch.
sentences.zh: 而且她留下的君主制基础，可能比1950年代以后的任何其他君主在位时看起来都要稳固。

sentences.en: It's hard to imagine how somebody could have left it in a better state, as it were.
sentences.zh: 很难想象还有谁能把它留在一个更好的状态。

sentences.en: So, yes, but she is boring.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，但她很无聊。

sentences.en: I mean, you were saying this is partly a tournament about iconography and about are you iconic?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你刚才说这在某种程度上是一场关于偶像地位的比赛，关于你是否具有偶像特质？

sentences.en: Are you remembered?
sentences.zh: 你会被人们记住吗？

sentences.en: I think the Queen is iconic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得女王是偶像。

sentences.en: Well, she is iconic, but she's iconic for stability, for seriousness, for responsibility, for duty, all admirable things, but not sexy things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她是偶像，但她代表的是稳定、严肃、责任和义务，这些都是令人钦佩的品质，但并不性感。

sentences.en: But she's globally iconic.
sentences.zh: 但她是全球性的偶像。

sentences.en: She is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, if you say the Queen, you know, there are lots of things, but everyone knows.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你提到女王，你知道，虽然有很多说法，但每个人都知道她。

sentences.en: Well, as you and I were talking about just the other day, not on the podcast, the fact that this,
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像你我前几天在播客之外谈到的那样，事实上，

sentences.en: the Athelstan result was being reported in kind of Indonesian news websites saying, you know, the Queen didn't win.
sentences.zh: 埃塞尔斯坦的结果被印尼的新闻网站报道了，说，你知道，女王没赢。

sentences.en: I mean, why would they care?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们为什么要在意？

sentences.en: They care because the Queen is iconic and is seen as a symbol of Britishness and actually becoming a symbol of the nation is what the monarchy, I mean, that's the sign of success,
sentences.zh: 他们在意是因为女王是偶像，被视为英国的象征，而成为国家的象征正是君主制成功的标志，

sentences.en: isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: And I think also that she has served as a kind of living reassurance to people that, you know, the country is still the country, that Britain is still Britain,
